text: AIDER SHIM: 0/14 surviving edits diagnosed 2026-08-19. UPDATE 2026-08-19 after all three plan steps completed: (1) Instrumentation BUILT AND PROVED: three border crossing emissions (arrival, departure, return) in interceptor.py's completion() — the blind segment now captures every kwarg aider sends, what we forward, and what comes back. (2) Sharp template INTEGRATED: the terse system prompt from peculiar-ragdoll/Qwen-Sharp-Chat-Templates is injected at the interceptor's seam (appended to system message or inserted as new one), because hex's qwen3-coder uses ollama's native RENDERER not a Jinja2 template. Temperature forwarding FIXED: aider's temperature kwarg now rides the options dict to inference_domain. (3) First instrumented drive COMPLETED and trail READ. FINDINGS FROM THE TRAIL: the model (qwen3-coder:30b on hex) DID RESPOND — two asks succeeded (18583 and 5423 prompt_eval tokens, ~5k char responses each), reflection loop ran (num_reflections=1). The model produced SEARCH/REPLACE blocks but they TARGETED THE WRONG FILE: the editable was test_driver.py, the model's patches were for driver.py code. hashes_moved=[] because none of the SEARCH blocks matched. The third ask (87k chars, 14 messages) timed out at 120s. REMAINING FACTORS: (a) the model confuses which file to edit in diff format — brief quality or edit_format issue; (b) the 120s transport timeout kills long conversations; (c) the brief is 16k chars of Cairn vocabulary the model never saw in training; (d) max_reflections=1 caps retry at one. The original diagnosis stands but the instrumentation has SHARPENED it: the survival problem is not temperature or prompt engineering — it is that the model produces syntactically correct SEARCH/REPLACE blocks aimed at the WRONG content.
